source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And when he had finished [or: completed] these words in the hearing of the people, he entered into the village of Nachum [Capernaum, village of consolation]

translation_notes: אלה (consonants אלה): Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, in context 'these the words' — אלה here functions as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (commonly אלה without Strong's separate entry, but often grouped under H428). H426 'God' doesn't fit 'God the words in ears of the people.' The demonstrative 'these' is the only reading that produces coherent syntax.

בכפר (consonants כפר): Candidates: H3722 'to cover/expiate', H3723 'a village', H3724 'a cover/village', H3725 'expiation', H6499 'a bullock'. A village reading fits perfectly before the place name Nachum.
נחום (consonants נחום): Candidates: H5149 'Nechum (name)', H5150 'consolation', H5151 'Nachum (prophet)'. As a place name 'Kfar Nachum' (Capernaum), H5151 fits as the proper name component.
textual_notes: אלה is parsed here as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (typically H428), but the candidates provided only list H421-H426. None of those fits the syntax; the demonstrative reading is contextually certain but not represented in the candidate list.
נכנס has no Strong's candidates provided; it appears to be a later Hebrew hitpael/nifal form of כנס (to gather/enter), not standard Biblical Hebrew vocabulary.

verses.literal: And when he completed these the words in [the] ears of the people he entered into [the] village [of] Nachum

verses.translation: And a servant of a captain of a hundred was very ill, to the point that he was declining toward death, gravely afflicted from a disease [or: evil sickness]. The influence [of the illness upon] his — he and everything about him — and that servant was very precious [or: valued] to him

translation_notes: ועבד (consonants עבד): Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do/make', H5649 'a servant', H5650 'a servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'a deed'. Context requires a noun — 'a servant of a captain' — so H5650 'servant' fits.
שר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/captain', H8270 'a string/umbilical cord'. 'Captain of a hundred' is a well-known military rank; H8269 is the clear choice.
היה (first instance): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. 'Was very sick' requires the copula verb; H1961.

מרע (both instances): Candidates: H4827 'wickedness', H4828 'a friend', H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'a crash', H7453 'an associate', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. In context of illness and dying, H7451 'evil/bad' as a noun meaning 'sickness/affliction' fits. The repetition מרע מרע appears to be an intensification or scribal notation.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Pronoun 'he' fits; H1931.
textual_notes: The phrase מרע מרע is unusual — the repetition may be an intensifier ('exceedingly evil/sick'), a scribal error (dittography), or two different readings (e.g., 'from an evil friend' vs. 'from evil upon evil').
מהשפעת appears to be a late Hebrew word (from שפע, 'influence/abundance') not in classical Biblical Hebrew Strong's lexicon.

הפההלב and הלבהפה appear corrupted or are compound expressions possibly meaning 'the mouth-the heart' and 'the heart-the mouth' — possibly describing symptoms or the nature of the disease. The text here may be damaged.
מרגליי appears to be a form of מרגלית (precious/pearl) or related to רגל with a meaning of 'valued/precious.' No Strong's candidates were provided.

verses.literal: And [a] servant [of a] captain [of a] hundred was very sick until he inclined to death from evil from evil from the influence of the — the — him he and all and him [the] servant was very precious to him

verses.translation: And when this [man] heard that Yeshua [salvation] was there, he sent to him elders [or: wise men] of the Jews, requesting him to come and heal his servant

translation_notes: זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. 'And when this [one] heard' — demonstrative pronoun fits; H2088.
שמע (consonants שמע): Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8086 'to hear (Aramaic)', H8087-H8090 (names/nouns). A verb 'heard' is needed; H8085.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/authority', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. 'Yeshua was there' is the natural reading; H8033.
שלח (consonants שלח): Candidates: H7971 'to send', H7972 'to send (Aramaic)', H7973 'spear/branch', H7974 'Shelach', H7975 'Shiloach'. 'He sent to him' requires the verb; H7971.
מבקש (consonants בקש): Candidates: H1245 'to search out/request', H7179 'straw'. 'Requesting him' fits perfectly; H1245.
textual_notes: חכמי (wise men of) has no Strong's candidates provided. This could be from H2450 חכם (wise). The parallel tradition uses 'elders of the Jews' — this text says 'wise men of the Jews,' which may reflect a different source or translation choice.

verses.literal: And when this [one] heard that Yeshua was there he sent to him wise [men] of the Yehudim requesting him that he would come that he would heal his servant

verses.translation: And those who came to Yeshua earnestly implored [or: entreated] his face [his presence] with urgency, saying to him: You are worthy to grant this to them

translation_notes: אתה (consonants אתה): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Context 'worthy you that you give' — second person pronoun; H859.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative 'this' fits; H2088.
להם: Candidates listed: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Preposition ל + pronoun הם = 'to them'; H1992.
textual_notes: חילו could be from חיל (H2342, to entreat/writhe) or חול (to be in anguish/implore). Without Strong's candidates provided, I read it as 'entreated' based on context of earnest appeal.
ראוי ('worthy/fitting') is a later Hebrew form not in the classical Strong's lexicon.

verses.literal: And those who came to Yeshua entreated his face with haste saying to him worthy [are] you that you give this to them

verses.translation: For he is beloved among [or: by] our people, and he built for us the house of assembly [the synagogue]

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for/because/that'. Causal 'for' fits; H3588.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Pronoun 'he' as subject; H1931.
בנה: Candidates: H1129 'to build', H5089 'lamentation'. 'He built for us' is coherent; H1129.
בית: Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 'a house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith', H3487 'object marker'. 'House of the assembly' = synagogue; H1004.
textual_notes: הכנסת (the assembly/synagogue) is a post-biblical Hebrew term (from כנס, to gather). It has no Strong's number in the classical lexicon.

עמנו could be parsed as עם (H5971 'people') + נו (our) = 'our people', or as עם (H5973 'with') + נו (us) = 'with us'. Both produce coherent readings: 'loved by our people' or 'loved with us.' I chose 'our people' as the more natural reading with אהוב.

verses.literal: For he [is] loved [among] our people and he built for us [the] house of the assembly

verses.translation: And Yeshua was walking with them, and when he was near to the house of the captain of the hundred, [the captain] sent to him his friends [or: loved ones] to say to Yeshua: Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy that you should enter under the shadow [or: shelter] of my roof-beam

translation_notes: אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H409 'not', H410 'strength/God', H411 'these', H412 'these', H413 'to/near'. Before an imperfect verb תרצה, H408 'do not' (negative command) fits perfectly.

תרצה: The only candidate listed is H8656 'Tirtsah (place name)'. However, the consonants תרצה also match the verb form from רצה (H7521, to desire/be pleased), 2ms imperfect. In context 'do not desire to trouble yourself,' this is clearly a verbal form meaning 'desire/wish.'
בצל (consonants בצל/צל): Candidates: H1211 'an onion', H6738 'shade'. 'In the shade of my beam' = under my roof; H6738 'shade' is the coherent choice. 'In an onion of my beam' makes no sense.
שלח: Candidates: H7971 'to send', H7973 'spear', H7974 'Shelach', H7975 'Shiloach'. 'He sent to him his friends'; H7971.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Direct address 'Lord' fits; H113.
textual_notes: תרצה is listed only as H8656 (place name Tirtsah), but the consonants clearly support a 2ms imperfect of רצה (H7521, to desire). The candidate list appears incomplete.
קורתי (my beam/rafter) appears to be from קורה (beam/rafter, H6982), with 1cs suffix. 'Under the shadow of my roof-beam' is an idiom for 'under my roof.'
להצטער is a hitpael infinitive of צער (to be distressed/troubled), a post-biblical form not in Strong's.
איניני appears to be a doubled negation form אין + אני (I am not), characteristic of later Hebrew.

verses.literal: And Yeshua walking with them and when he was near to [the] house [of the] captain [of] the hundred he sent to him his loved ones that they would say to Yeshua Lord do not desire to trouble yourself for I am not worthy that you enter in [the] shade of my beam

verses.translation: And because of this I did not consider [or: reckon] myself worthy to come to you, but [or: rather, yet] speak this [only] in words, and my servant [or: son] will be healed

translation_notes: מדמה (consonants דמה): Candidates: H1819 'to compare/consider/liken', H1820 'to be dumb/silent/perish', H1821 'to resemble', H1822 'desolation'. 'I consider/reckon that I would be worthy' — H1819 fits as 'to consider/reckon.'
אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. As an adversative conjunction 'but/yet'; H61.

ובני: Candidates listed: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. However, the consonants בני naturally parse as בן (H1121, son) + י (my) = 'my son.' This reading fits: 'and my son/servant will be healed.' The candidate list appears incomplete.
textual_notes: מדמה could be read as a negative construction if a negation was lost or implied — 'I did not consider myself worthy to come to you' — which fits the broader narrative logic better (the centurion's humility). However, the text as written lacks an explicit negative. The phrase may be elliptical.
ובני could mean 'my son' (בן + י) or 'my builder' or could be the name Bani. 'My son' or 'my servant/boy' fits the context of someone being healed.

verses.literal: And on account of this I consider that I would be worthy that I come to you but say this in words and my son will be healed

verses.translation: For I [am] a man who has [those] under my authority and under my power — horsemen [or: soldiers] — and I say to this one: Go! and he goes; and I say to another: Come! and he comes; and I say to my servant: Do this! and he does it

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. 'I am a man' — H120.
שיש (consonants שיש): Candidates: H7893 'marble/white', H3426 'there is/are'. 'A man that there is to me' = 'who has'; H3426.
לזה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. 'To this one: Go!' — H2088.
לאחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'another/next', H313 'Acher (name)'. 'To another: Come!' — H312.
לעבדי: Only candidate H5660 'Abdi (name)'. But consonants עבד+י clearly = 'my servant' (H5650 + 1cs suffix). The candidate list is incomplete; I use H5650.
textual_notes: כחי could be parsed as כח (H3581, strength/power) + י (my) = 'my power', or as consonants כחי from H2416 חי (alive) with כ prefix = 'like my life.' 'My power' fits the context of military authority.
פרשים could be from פרש (H6571, horseman) or פרש (H6567, to separate/declare). 'Horsemen/cavalry' fits a military commander's description; soldiers under command.
ואומר: The only candidate listed is H201 'Omar (name)'. This is clearly a participle of אמר (H559, to say) — 'and saying/I say.' The candidate list is incomplete.

verses.literal: For I [am] a man that there is to me under my authority and under my power horsemen and saying I to this go and he goes and saying I to another come and he comes and saying I to my servant do this and he does it

verses.translation: And when Yeshua heard that word [or: matter], he was astonished, and he turned around and said: Truly I say to you — I have not found faithfulness [or: trust, firmness of faith] like this in Israel

translation_notes: הדבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak/arrange', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'a pasture'. 'That word/matter' — H1697.
שמע: Candidates: H8085 'to hear', H8086-H8090. Verb 'heard'; H8085.
ותמה (consonants תמה): Candidates: H8538 'innocence', H8539 'to be in consternation/astonished', H8540 'a miracle'. 'He was astonished'; H8539.
ואמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-H564. 'And said'; H559.
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Simple negation; H3808.

verses.literal: And that the word heard Yeshua and he was astonished and he turned and said truth I saying to you not have I found faithfulness like this in Israel

verses.translation: And those who had been sent to Yeshua returned to the house and found the young servant who had been ill — [the illness] had ceased, for he had been healed and [was] healthy [or: robust]

translation_notes: אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H412 'these', H413 'to/near'. Directional 'to the house'; H413.
הבית (consonants בית): Candidates: H1004 'a house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith', H3487 'object marker'. 'The house'; H1004.
הנער (consonants נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/youth/servant', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. 'The youth/young servant'; H5288.
שהיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah'. 'Who was/had been'; H1961.
אפס (consonants אפס): Candidates: H656 'to disappear/cease', H657 'cessation/end'. 'Ceased [being ill]' — the verb H656 fits: the illness had ceased.
ובריא (consonants בריא): H1277 'fatted/plump'. In context of recovery from illness, this means 'healthy/robust'; H1277.
textual_notes: The syntax שהיה אפס שנתרפא is ambiguous: it could mean 'who had formerly been [ill but] had now ceased [being ill], having been healed' or 'who had been at the point of ending [dying] but was healed.' I read אפס as indicating the illness ceased/disappeared.
שנשתלחו is a nishtafel/hitpael passive of שלח — 'who were sent' — a later Hebrew form.

verses.literal: And they returned to the house those who were sent to Yeshua and they found the youth who was [had] ceased being sick and healed and healthy

verses.translation: And it came to pass [or: happened] from that point onward that Yeshua was walking toward a city called Naim [Pleasant], and his disciples and a great [crowd of] people were going with him
words: and it was done / and it came to be

translation_notes: היה (H1961 vs H1962): H1961 'to exist, come to pass' vs H1962 'ruin'. The sentence describes a narrative event beginning, so H1961 fits naturally as 'it came to pass.'

בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher', H5895 'young ass'. The phrase 'going to a ___ called Naim' requires a place; H5892 'city' is the only coherent reading.
נעים (H5273): Only candidate is 'delightful/pleasant.' This functions here as a proper place name (Naim), which itself means 'pleasant.'
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with'. Preceded by 'ורוב' (and a multitude of), this must be a noun — 'people' (H5971).
textual_notes: ונעשה has no Strong's candidates provided; it appears to be a Mishnaic/later Hebrew reflexive-passive form (ונעשה from עשה) meaning 'and it was done / it came about.' No Strong's number assigned.
ואילך is a post-biblical Hebrew expression meaning 'and onward/further'; no Strong's candidates provided.

verses.literal: And it came to be from here and onward that Yeshua was going to a city called Naim and his disciples and a multitude of people going with him

verses.translation: And when Yeshua approached [or: drew near to] the gate of the city, behold, [they were] carrying out a dead [man], one [only son], who was the son of a widow, and she had no [other child] besides, and a great [crowd of] people from the city were walking with that woman

translation_notes: וכאשר: The conjunction וכ + אשר. Candidates include H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness'. In narrative context introducing a temporal clause ('and when...'), H834 is the clear choice.

קרב: Candidates: H7126 'to approach', H7128 'hostile encounter', H7130 'the center/midst', H7131 'near'. The subject is Yeshua moving toward the gate; H7126 'to approach' produces the most natural image.
בשער: Candidates: H8175 'to storm', H8179 'a gate/door', H8177 'hair', etc. Combined with 'the city,' H8179 'gate' is the only coherent reading — cities have gates.
העיר: H5892 'city' vs H5894 'watcher' vs H5895 'young ass'. Following 'the gate of the ___,' H5892 'city' is the natural reading.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. As a narrative interjection introducing a dramatic scene (a funeral procession), H2009 'behold' fits perfectly.
מת (H4962): Only candidate 'an adult/man' but the consonants מת in context clearly mean 'dead [person]' (from the root מות). H4962 is the nominal form used here to mean a dead man.
אחד: H258 'to unify' vs H259 'one/first'. As an adjective modifying the dead man, H259 'one' fits — indicating a sole/only [son].
שהיה: H1961 'to be/exist' vs H1962 'ruin'. Relative clause 'who was a son' requires a copulative verb; H1961.
עוד: H5749 'to testify' vs H5750 'again/more/still'. After 'there was not to her,' H5750 'any more' is the natural adverbial reading.
ורב: H7227 'abundant/great' vs H7228 'archer'. Describing a crowd, H7227 is clearly correct.
עם (first): H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with'. After 'ורב' (a multitude of), it must be the noun 'people' (H5971).
מן: H4478 'manna' vs H4480 'from/out of'. Preceding 'the city,' H4480 'from' is the only coherent reading.
עם (second): H5971 'people' vs H5973 'with'. Before 'that woman,' this must be the preposition 'with' (H5973).
textual_notes: הא<ה appears to have a damaged/missing consonant (indicated by <). The context strongly suggests אשה (woman), referring to the widow. The reading 'the woman' is contextually certain but the text is physically damaged.
ההיא is a feminine demonstrative 'that one' — here modifying the woman. No Strong's candidates were provided.

verses.literal: And when Yeshua drew near to the gate of the city behold [they were] carrying a dead one who was [the] son of a widow and there was not to her [any] more and a multitude of people from the city [were] going with that woman

verses.translation: And when Yeshua saw her, he was moved [stirred, shaken] with compassion [loyal-kindness, tender mercy] over her, and Yeshua said to her: Do not weep
words: she saw him / he saw her

translation_notes: וכאשר: H834 'when' — temporal conjunction introducing the scene, same as section 2.
היה: H1961 'to be/exist' vs H1962 'ruin'. Auxiliary verb describing Yeshua's state: 'he was moved'; H1961.

בחסד: H2616 'to be kind/bow', H2617 'kindness/lovingkindness/compassion', H2618 'Chesed (name)'. The preposition ב + noun describing the emotional quality; H2617 'compassion/kindness' produces the coherent image of being moved with tender mercy.
אמר: H559 'to say' vs H561 'something said' vs H563 'a lamb'. As a verb with Yeshua as subject and speech following, H559 'to say' is the clear reading.
אל: H408 'not (deprecative)' vs H410 'God/mighty' vs H413 'to/toward'. Before the imperfect תבכי, H408 is the standard negative particle for prohibitions: 'do not.'

עליה: H5944 'something lofty/upper room'. However, the consonants על + יה naturally parse as the preposition 'upon/over' + 3fs suffix 'her.' The Strong's entry H5944 is for the noun עליה, but here the context demands the prepositional reading 'upon her / over her.'
textual_notes: ראתה could be parsed as 'she saw' (3fs perfect of ראה with paragogic ה) or as 'he saw her' (3ms perfect of ראה + 3fs object suffix). The narrative flow suggests Yeshua is the one seeing the widow and being moved to compassion, so 'he saw her' is more likely. However, the form ראתה is morphologically more natural as 3fs 'she saw.' The subsequent clause makes Yeshua the subject of the emotional response, which works with either parsing.

נע has no Strong's candidates provided. The consonants נע could derive from נוע (H5128 'to waver, move, shake') or be related to a Mishnaic usage meaning 'moved/stirred.' In context — 'he was moved in compassion' — it describes an emotional stirring.

verses.literal: And when Yeshua saw her he was moved in compassion over her and Yeshua said to her do not weep

verses.translation: And Yeshua drew near and touched the bier [or: stretcher, bed], and those carrying him stopped [stood still]. And Yeshua said: Young man, I command [you] to rise up. This [is] a word [or: matter] like this — those who were sent [or: dispatched] — [the one who] was healed from there

translation_notes: קרב: H7126 'to approach' vs H7128 'hostile encounter' vs H7130 'center'. Yeshua is physically moving toward the bier; H7126 'to approach' fits.
ונגע: H5060 'to touch/lay the hand upon' vs H5061 'a blow/affliction'. The action is physical contact with the bier; H5060 'to touch' is the natural reading.

המטה: Candidates: H4294 'rod/staff/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'a bed/bier/litter', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. In the context of a funeral procession where bearers are carrying a dead man, H4296 'bier/litter' produces the only coherent image.
נער: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble', H5288 'a boy/young man', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Yeshua is addressing the dead son directly; H5288 'young man' is the natural vocative.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship/fleet'. The speaker is identifying himself as the one commanding; H589 'I' is obvious.
מצוה: H4687 'a command (noun)' vs H6680 'to command/constitute (verb)'. After 'I,' a verb is expected; H6680 as a participle 'commanding' — 'I [am] commanding' — fits the syntax.
דבר: H1696 'to speak' vs H1697 'a word/matter/thing' vs H1698 'pestilence'. In context describing 'this ___ like this,' the noun H1697 'matter/thing' is the coherent choice.
משם: H8033 'there' (with prefix מ = 'from there') vs H8034 'a name'. The prepositional reading 'from there' fits the concluding clause.
textual_notes: The final clause 'זו דבר כזאת אותם שנשלחו שנרפא משם' is syntactically difficult. It may be a summary or narrator's comment rather than part of Yeshua's direct speech. One possible reading: 'This [is] a matter like this [regarding] those who were sent out — that [one who] was healed from there.' Another parsing: it could describe the report being sent out about the healing. The text is genuinely ambiguous at this point.

שנרפא could be parsed as 'that he was healed' (nifal perfect of רפא) or 'that he healed' (with the ש as a relative pronoun). The nifal (passive) reading 'was healed' seems more natural given the dead man being raised.
שנשלחו — 'who were sent out' — the referent is unclear. It could refer to messengers, or to the words/reports being sent out about the miracle.

verses.literal: And Yeshua approached and touched the bier and those carrying him stood [still] and Yeshua said young man I command that you rise this [is the] matter like this those who were sent [out] that [one] was healed from there

verses.translation: And immediately [at once] that one who had been dead rose up and began to speak, and they returned [restored] him to his mother

translation_notes: שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the relative clause 'who was dead' requires a copulative verb, not 'ruin'.

לדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the lamed prefix indicates an infinitive 'to speak', fitting the context of someone rising and beginning to talk.
textual_notes: מת: Only H4962 is listed ('an adult, a man'), but the consonants מת clearly also function as the adjective/participle 'dead' in Hebrew. The context demands 'dead' — one who was dead rose and spoke. The Strong's listing appears incomplete for this form.

verses.literal: And immediately that one who was dead rose and began to speak and they returned [him] to his mother

verses.translation: And all the peoples saw [experienced] a great fear [awe, reverence] and they praised and blessed God, [saying]: A great prophet has risen in our midst, for YHWH has visited [attended to, cared for] his people

translation_notes: רי או: The consonants רי (H7377 'irrigation/shower') and או (H176 'or') standing alone make no contextual sense. These consonants likely represent ראו — 'they saw' — with a scribal separation. The full phrase 'all the peoples saw a great fear' is coherent.

האל (אל): Candidates: H408/H409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because the article ה + אל = 'the God', and the context is praising and blessing, which requires a divine object.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because the clause introduces a reason for praise.
נביא: Candidates: H5029 'a prophet', H5030 'a prophet/inspired man'. Both are essentially identical; chose H5030 as the more common form.
textual_notes: רי או appears to be a scribal splitting of ראו ('they saw'). The word division in the consonantal text is ambiguous here.
The [] marker appears to indicate a lacuna or editorial insertion point in the manuscript, likely where 'saying' or 'lēmor' would appear.

verses.literal: And all the peoples saw fear great and they praised and they blessed God [saying] a prophet great has risen in our midst for YHWH has visited his people

verses.translation: And this word [report, matter] spread throughout all the land of Judah

translation_notes: וזה (זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because the demonstrative pronoun 'this' fits as a modifier of 'the word/report'.

הדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'the word/report was scattered' describes the spreading of news.

verses.literal: And this the word was scattered in all [the] land [of] Judah

verses.translation: And [the] disciples went to Yochanan [John] and told him all these things [words, matters]

translation_notes: אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation', H424 'an oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. None of these match the obvious demonstrative pronoun אלה ('these'), which is extremely common in Hebrew but apparently not listed among the candidates. The context 'all these the words' clearly requires the demonstrative pronoun.
textual_notes: אלה: The demonstrative pronoun 'these' is not among the Strong's candidates provided, yet the context unmistakably requires it. This is likely an omission in the candidate list.

verses.literal: And disciples went to Yochanan and said to him all these the words

verses.translation: And Yochanan [John] called [summoned] two of his disciples and sent them to Yeshua [Joshua/Jesus]

translation_notes: קרא: Candidates: H7121 'to call out to/address/summon', H7122 'to encounter', H7123 'to call (Aramaic)', H7124 'a partridge'. Chose H7121 because the action of summoning disciples fits perfectly.
ושלחם: The root is שלח 'to send' with suffix ם 'them'. The candidates listed under לחם are irrelevant; the word parses as ו+שלח+ם.

verses.literal: And Yochanan called two from his disciples and sent them to Yeshua

verses.translation: And they said to him: Are you he — the one who is destined [prepared, about] to come — or [should] we be hoping [waiting] for another?

translation_notes: אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you'. Chose H859 because the sentence structure 'you he [are] the one' requires a pronoun.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/the same', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 because it functions as a copulative pronoun identifying the subject.
שעתיד: Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/future/treasure'. Chose H6264 because 'the one prepared/destined to come' fits the messianic expectation context.

אחר: Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'another/other', H313 'Acher (name)'. Chose H312 because 'hoping for another' makes contextual sense as the alternative to the expected one.

verses.literal: And they said to him you he [are] that one who [is] destined to come or we [are] hoping [for] another

verses.translation: And Yeshua answered and said to them: Go and report what you have seen and heard — the blind are seeing, the lame are walking, the lepers are cleansed [purified], the deaf are hearing, the dead have risen [to] life, and the poor are being told [the good news, proclaimed to]

translation_notes: וענה (ענה): Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to respond (Aramaic)', H6033 'to afflict (Aramaic)', H6034 'Anah (name)'. Chose H6030 because 'answered and said' is a standard Hebrew narrative formula.

ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because it is the standard verb 'and he said'.
להם: Listed candidate H3859 'to burn/rankle' is irrelevant; this is the preposition ל + pronoun הם (H1992) 'to them'.
החרשים: H2798 'mechanics/craftsmen (valley name)' is listed, but the consonants חרש also yield 'deaf' (from חרש meaning deaf/silent). Context of healing miracles demands 'the deaf'.
ץראיתם: Appears to be a scribal variant of ראיתם ('you have seen') with a prefixed ץ possibly a scribal artifact or abbreviation.
textual_notes: ץראיתם: The initial ץ is anomalous. It may be a scribal error, abbreviation, or damaged text. The core form ראיתם ('you saw/have seen') is clear from context.

מוגדים: This form is unusual. It appears to be a passive participle from a root related to נגד (to tell, announce) in a causative/passive form — 'being told/announced to'. The exact morphological derivation is uncertain.
החרשים: The Strong's candidate offered (H2798 'mechanics/valley name') does not fit. The consonants חרש also mean 'deaf' in Hebrew, which the healing-list context requires.

verses.literal: And answered Yeshua and said to them go and say what you have seen and you have heard the blind [are] seeing the lame [are] walking the lepers [are] clean the deaf [are] hearing the dead have risen alive and the poor [are] told [the good news]

verses.translation: And blessed [fortunate] will be those who will not be denying [rejecting, disbelieving] in me

translation_notes: בי: The candidate H994 'oh that!/if it please' does not fit. The consonants ב+י simply mean 'in me' (preposition ב + first person suffix). Context of denying/rejecting requires 'in me'.
textual_notes: כופרים: From root כפר which can mean 'to cover/atone' (H3722) or 'to deny/disbelieve'. In this context the meaning is clearly 'denying/disbelieving' — those who reject or refuse to believe.

verses.literal: And blessed will be those who not will be denying in me

verses.translation: And when the messengers [emissaries] of Yochanan [John] were returning, he began to say to the peoples: Why did you go out to see in the wilderness [open land]? Reeds [rushes] shaking [swaying] in every wind [direction]?

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ+אשר = 'as/when', a standard temporal conjunction.
לאמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562-H564. Chose H559 because ל+אמר is the standard infinitive 'to say/saying'.

במדבר: H4057 'wilderness/desert/open field' fits perfectly as the location one goes out to see something. The sub-candidates for דבר are irrelevant when the full form מדבר is recognized as 'wilderness'.

מושבים: This could derive from שוב ('to return') in a passive/causative form, or from ישב ('to sit/dwell'). Given the context — the messengers of Yochanan departing — 'returning' fits better than 'seated'.
textual_notes: מושבים: Could be parsed as from שוב ('returning') or ישב ('seated/dwelling'). The narrative context of messengers leaving favors 'returning', but 'departing/going back' is also possible.

הץוקים: The ץ prefix is anomalous (as in section 7). This likely represents קנים or a similar word for 'reeds'. The exact form is uncertain — possibly a scribal convention in this manuscript for representing a tsade-initial or qoph-initial word.
שנועות: Appears to be a participle from נוע ('to shake/sway/wander'). The ש prefix is the relative particle. The feminine plural form matches 'reeds' (which are grammatically feminine).

verses.literal: And when were returning messengers [of] Yochanan he began to say to the peoples why did you go out to see in the wilderness the reeds shaking to every wind

verses.translation: But what sort of things did you go out to see? And [did] all the peoples [expect] a man dressed in an abundance of garments? Behold, those who dress themselves in precious [costly] clothing and in luxury [delight] — behold them [as] kings in their houses [palaces]!
words: and the peoples all of them

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the adversative conjunction 'but/yet' introduces a contrasting question after the previous one about reeds.
אי: Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because combined with זה it forms the interrogative 'what kind/which sort'.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because אי זה together means 'what kind of' — an interrogative phrase.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because 'behold those who dress in costly clothing' is a natural presentative exclamation.
הנם: H2011 'Hinnom (a Jebusite)' does not fit. This is הנ+ם = 'behold them' (הנה with 3mp suffix). The context of pointing to kings in their houses requires a demonstrative.
textual_notes: הנם: The only Strong's candidate (H2011 'Hinnom') is a place name that does not fit. This form is best parsed as הנה + ם (behold them), a suffixed presentative particle.
והעמיםכלם appears to be a run-together scribal form of והעמים כלם ('and the peoples all of them').

The syntax of this verse is complex. It could be read as two questions ('What did you go out to see? A man clothed in many garments?') followed by a declarative contrast ('Behold, those in costly clothes — they are kings in their houses').

verses.literal: But what kind [of] matters did you go out to see and the peoples all of them a man clothed from abundance [of] garments behold those who clothed themselves in garments precious and in luxury behold them kings in their houses

verses.translation: But [truly], what [is] this matter [for which] you went out to see? A prophet? I say to you — and even more [or: beyond, exceeding] than a prophet.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because the context is a rhetorical address transitioning to a question — an adversative conjunction 'but/yet' fits naturally.

אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because combined with זה דבר it forms a question 'where is this thing' or 'what is this thing', fitting the rhetorical questioning pattern.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'thing/matter' fits naturally as the object of 'where is this' in a rhetorical question about purpose.

אומר (consonants אומר): The only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar' (a proper name), but contextually this is clearly a participle from אמר (to say), functioning as 'saying/I say'. The lexicon listing is incomplete for this verbal form.
textual_notes: אי זה דבר could be parsed as 'where [is] this thing' (interrogative) or as a compound 'what kind of thing.' The phrase אי זה together commonly functions as 'which/what' in later Hebrew.

אומר is listed only as H201 (Omar, proper name) in the candidates, but in context it is unmistakably a qal participle of אמר 'to say.' No Strong's number for the verb form was provided among candidates.

verses.literal: Yet where [is] this thing [you] went out to see? A prophet? [I am] saying to you and still more than a prophet.

verses.translation: This is [the one] about whom [it is] written: Behold, I [am] sending my messenger [or: my angel] before your face, who will prepare [or: establish] the way before you.

translation_notes: הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because this introduces a proclamation formula — 'Behold, I am sending' is a coherent announcement.

מלאכי (consonants מלאכי): The candidate H4401 is 'Malachi' the prophet name, but the consonants מלאכי literally mean 'my messenger' (from מלאך + 1cs suffix). In context, 'I am sending my messenger' is the coherent reading. The Strong's number H4401 covers both the proper name and the possessive form.
הדרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread/walk', H1870 'road/way/path'. Chose H1870 because with the article ה it functions as a noun 'the way,' which fits as the object of 'prepare.'
textual_notes: שולח has no verb root candidates listed (only לח 'fresh'), but it is clearly a qal participle of שלח 'to send.' The lexicon candidates are incomplete here.

שיכין is listed only with H3199 'Jakin' (proper name), but in context it is a hiphil imperfect of כון 'to establish/prepare' with the relative prefix ש-. No appropriate Strong's for the verb was provided.
מלאכי simultaneously evokes the prophet Malachi (H4401) and the literal meaning 'my messenger' — both are valid and may be intentionally dual.

verses.literal: This [is he] that about him [is] written: Look I [am] sending to you my messenger before your face that will prepare the way before your face.

verses.translation: For I say to you, that among all who have been born in the world from a woman, none has been born greater than Yochanan the Immerser [or: the Baptizer]. But whoever is least [or: smallest] in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Chose H61 'but/yet' because it introduces a contrast between the greatness of Yochanan and the status of the least in the kingdom.

קטן (consonants קטן): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'small/diminutive', H6997 'Katan (name)'. Chose H6996 because 'small/least' as an adjective fits the contrast with 'greater.'
שהוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 because 'whoever he [is]' uses the pronoun as a copula.

טבול (consonants טבול): H2871 'dyed/turban'. The consonants טבל relate to 'dipping/immersing' (cf. H2881 טבל 'to dip'). Here טבול appears to function as an epithet 'the Immerser/Baptizer,' derived from the root טבל. H2871 is the closest match though its primary gloss is 'turban (dyed)' — the root meaning of immersion/dyeing is shared.
שמים (consonants שמים): Candidates: H8064 'sky/heaven', H4325 'water', H3220 'sea'. Chose H8064 because 'kingdom of heaven' is a coherent and well-attested phrase.
textual_notes: מא<ה appears to contain a corrupted or damaged consonant (<). It likely reads מאשה 'from a woman' (אשה H802), describing those born of women.
טבול is glossed as 'turban/dyed' (H2871) but functions here as an epithet from the root טבל 'to dip/immerse.' This is a denominative use not fully captured by the single Strong's entry provided.

verses.literal: For I [am] saying to you that in all who were born in [the] world from a woman not was born [one] greater than Yochanan [the] Immerser but whoever he [is] small in [the] kingdom [of] heaven [is] greater than him.

verses.translation: And all the people, including the worldly [or: common, secular] ones, when they heard this, were immersed [or: baptized] in the immersion [or: baptism] of Yochanan.

translation_notes: העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'people/tribe', H5972 'people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5971 because 'all the people' with the article makes natural sense as a collective noun.
הם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'they were immersed' is the coherent subject-verb pairing.
שזה (consonants זה): H2088 'this'. With the relative prefix ש-, it reads 'that this' or 'who this,' functioning as a relative clause marker.
textual_notes: והעולמיים is a later Hebrew formation not found in biblical Strong's. It derives from עולם (H5769) with an adjectival suffix, meaning 'worldly ones' or 'people of the world' — likely referring to common people or those engaged with worldly affairs (possibly tax collectors or similar).
נטבלים and בטבילת are derived from the root טבל 'to dip/immerse' in a nithpael/hitpael form. No Strong's numbers are provided but the root is H2881.

verses.literal: And all the people and the worldly [ones] that this heard they [were] immersed in [the] immersion of Yochanan.

verses.translation: But the Perushim [Pharisees] and the sages [or: experts] of the law rejected [or: despised] among themselves the counsel of YHWH, in that they were not immersed by Yochanan.

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Chose H61 'but/yet' again as it introduces a contrast between the people who accepted immersion and the Pharisees who rejected it.

הדת (consonants דת): Candidates: H1881 'royal edict/statute', H1882 same. Chose H1881 because 'wise ones of the law/statute' describes legal experts, fitting the context of religious authority figures.
textual_notes: מבזים is a piel participle from בזה 'to despise/scorn' — not listed in candidates but the root is H959. The form indicates ongoing or characteristic action of despising.
עצת is the construct form of עצה 'counsel/plan' (H6098), not listed in candidates. 'The counsel of YHWH' refers to God's purpose or plan.
מיוחנן with the מ prefix could mean 'from Yochanan' or 'by Yochanan' — both are valid. 'By Yochanan' (agent) fits the passive verb נטבלים better.

verses.literal: But the Perushim and [the] wise [ones] of the law [were] despising among themselves [the] counsel of YHWH that not they were immersed by Yochanan.

verses.translation: Therefore, to whom shall I liken [or: compare] the people of this generation?

translation_notes: לכן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'thus/therefore', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because ל + כן forms the standard conjunction 'therefore,' which logically connects the preceding rejection to the following parable.

הדור (consonants דור): Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle/ball', H1755 'generation/age', H1756 'Dor (place)'. Chose H1755 because 'this generation' is the coherent reading with the demonstrative זה.
textual_notes: נאמר could be parsed as 1cp imperfect 'shall we say' or as niphal 'shall it be said.' Both work; the 1cp reading is slightly more natural as a rhetorical self-address.
נמשלים is a niphal participle from משל 'to compare/liken' (H4911), meaning 'are compared/likened.'

verses.literal: Therefore to whom shall [we] say [the] men of this generation [are] compared?

verses.translation: They are compared to children sitting in the marketplace, calling out to one another and saying: We played [music] for you with instruments [or: with musical instruments] and it was not pleasing to you. We wept, and you did not weep.

translation_notes: הם (consonants הם): Chose H1992 'they' as the subject of the comparison.

ערב (consonants ערב): Candidates: H6148 'to intermix/barter/pledge', H6149 'to be agreeable/pleasing', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6149 because 'it was not pleasing to you' perfectly describes the children's complaint that their companions did not respond to the music — a natural, coherent image of unresponsiveness.
ואתם (consonants אתם): H864 'Etham (place)' is the only candidate listed, but contextually this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you' (אתם). The lexicon candidates are incomplete.
textual_notes: ב<וק appears to have a damaged/uncertain consonant. It likely reads בשוק 'in the market/marketplace' (שוק H7784).
ניגון is not listed in Strong's candidates but derives from the root נגן 'to play music' (H5059). It means 'melody/music/playing.'
שרנו could be from שיר 'to sing' (H7891) — 'we sang' — which fits the context of children playing music and singing.
The phrase ולא ערב לכם is unusual. Instead of the expected 'you did not dance,' this text reads 'it was not pleasing to you,' which may represent a different textual tradition.

verses.literal: Compared they [are] to youths sitting in [the] market and speaking among them and saying we sang to you with instruments of music and not [it was] pleasing to you we [are] weeping and you are not weeping.

verses.translation: When Yochanan the Immerser [or: Baptizer] came, neither eating bread nor drinking wine, you said that he was possessed by a demon [or: driven mad by a spirit].

translation_notes: כאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר forms 'as when/just as,' introducing a temporal clause.

לחם (consonants לחם): Candidates: H3898 'to consume/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because 'not eating bread' describes abstinence from food, a coherent image of asceticism.
שהוא (consonants הוא): Chose H1931 'he' because 'that he [is] demonized' provides the subject for the accusation.
textual_notes: משוטן is a later Hebrew form meaning 'demonized/possessed by Satan/a demon,' derived from שטן (H7854 'adversary/Satan'). The מ- prefix with the passive/reflexive pattern indicates a state: 'one who has been made subject to a שטן.' No Strong's number was provided in candidates.
טבול as 'Immerser' — see note in section 3 about this epithet.

verses.literal: As when Yochanan [the] Immerser came not eating bread and not drinking wine and you said that he [is] demonized.

verses.translation: [The] Son of Man [or: the human one] came eating and drinking, and you say: Look — this person is a glutton [or: destroyer] and a friend [or: lover] of worldly people [or: sinners' companion] and of sinners.

translation_notes: בן (consonants בן): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of the human' is the well-known Hebraic idiom for a human being or the specific title 'Son of Man.'

האדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/gem'. Chose H120 for both occurrences — first as 'the human' in 'son of the human,' second as 'the man/this person' in the accusation.
הנה (consonants הנה): Chose H2009 'lo/behold' as it introduces the accusatory exclamation.
textual_notes: מחריב derives from the root חרב which can mean 'to destroy/lay waste' (H2717) or 'to dry up.' In context, as an accusation paired with eating and drinking, it likely means 'glutton/one who destroys (food)' — i.e., a voracious eater. This is an unusual word choice compared to expected forms.
ו]אוהב[ has brackets in the source text, indicating the scribe marked this as uncertain or a correction. It appears to be from אהב 'to love' (H157) — 'and a lover/friend of.'
העולמיים — same later Hebrew formation as in section 4, meaning 'worldly people' or 'people of the world,' likely parallel to 'sinners' in the following word.

verses.literal: Came [the] son of the human eating and drinking and you [are] saying look the human [is] a destroyer and [a lover] of the worldly [ones] and the sinners.

verses.translation: And wisdom [or: righteousness] is justified [or: vindicated] by [or: on account of] all her children.

translation_notes: והצדקה (consonants צדקה): Candidates: H6665 'beneficence', H6666 'rightness/righteousness/justice/virtue'. Chose H6666 because 'righteousness/justice' being 'justified by its children' produces a coherent proverbial statement about vindication through results.

בעד (consonants בעד): Candidates: H1157 'on behalf of/for/by', plus עד candidates H5703-H5708. Chose H1157 because 'justified on behalf of / by means of its children' makes sense — righteousness is proved right through its children/outcomes.
textual_notes: נצטדקה is a hitpael/nitpael form of צדק 'to be righteous/justified' — a reflexive-passive meaning 'was justified/vindicated itself.' This rare intensive form emphasizes the self-evident nature of the vindication.

בניו has a masculine 3rd person suffix ('his/its sons'), but צדקה is grammatically feminine. This may indicate that the suffix refers loosely to the concept ('its children') or reflects a scribal convention. Some traditions read 'her children' for wisdom/righteousness personified as female.
צדקה here may be functioning as a stand-in for 'wisdom' (חכמה), as parallel traditions of this saying use 'wisdom' in this position. However, the consonants clearly read צדקה 'righteousness.'

verses.literal: And the righteousness was justified on behalf of its sons.

verses.translation: And one of the Pharisees implored [or: beseeched] him that he would eat with him, and when Yeshua entered into the house of the Pharisee, they sat down at [the] table.

translation_notes: אחד (H258 vs H259): H258 = 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 = 'one/first'. In context 'one from the Pharisees' is a natural count, so H259 'one'.

חלה (H2470 vs H2471): H2470 in piel = 'to entreat, beseech (the face of someone)', H2471 = 'a cake'. With פניו 'his face' following, the idiom חלה פני = 'entreated his face' is coherent. A cake doesn't fit the syntax. Chose H2470.
וכאשר: אשר candidates — H834 'when/that' forms the conjunction כאשר 'when'. All other candidates (happiness, step, proper nouns) don't form this conjunction. Chose H834.

In context 'you not anointed my head with oil' is coherent; 'you not destroyed/disfigured my head' is forced. The listed candidates share consonants שחת (ruin) or חת (crushed), but the full consonantal string משחת best parses as a verbal form of משח (anoint) with 2ms suffix. None of the destruction/ruin candidates produce a coherent image with 'my head with oil'.

Chose H4888 as a verbal form from the root משח — she anointed. The noun 'unction' from H4888 also supports the anointing sense.

The consonants משיח are cognate with משח (anoint), yielding 'with anointing/ointment'.

The < may indicate a scribal insertion or lacuna. If the full word is בשמן, it reads 'with oil' which fits perfectly in context.

במשיחה: The consonants could theoretically parse as ב + משיחה (feminine form related to משיח 'anointed one/messiah'), yielding 'with anointing' as a substance or act. The listed candidates H7881-H7882 derive from שיח rather than משח, but the full consonantal string better supports the משח root. אל (second instance, before תפחד): Candidates: H408 'not', H413 'to.' Chose H408 because אל + imperfect = negative command 'do not fear.'
בטח (consonants ב-ט-ח): Candidates: H982 'to trust', H983 'place of refuge/safety', H984 'Betach.' Chose H982 because an imperative 'trust!' fits the exhortation context.
לשלום: H7965 'peace/welfare.' Standard blessing formula 'go in peace.'
textual_notes: The ] [ marks in the text appear to indicate a lacuna or editorial gap between the two episodes (the woman and the synagogue ruler's daughter).
הא'ה is again the damaged/abbreviated form of האשה 'the woman.'

ותהי נושעת — the subject could be 'you' (the father, addressed with feminine salvation?) or 'she' (the daughter). Given that the girl is the one who needs saving/healing, 'she will be saved' seems most likely, though the form could also be second person.
ביהוה — the manuscript explicitly uses the divine name YHWH, which is noteworthy for a text of this type.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to the woman your faith has saved you go to peace [ ] and Yeshua heard this and said to [the] father [of] the girl do not fear trust in YHWH and believe and you will be saved
